The graph above shows $y={g}^{″}(x).$ Find the intervals on which the function $g(x)$ is concave up.
feedback.worked_solution:
A function $g(x)$ is concave up over an interval $(a,b)$ if ${g}^{″}(x)>0$ for all $x\in (a,b).$

On the given graph of $y={g}^{″}(x)$, we can see that ${g}^{″}(x)>0$ on the intervals $(-\infty ,-3),$ $(-1,0),$ and $(1,3).$ Therefore, the function $g(x)$ is concave up on the intervals $(-\infty ,-3),$ $(-1,0),$ and $(1,3).$
